hypothesis: Idle cores executing WFI stop receiving time-slice SGIs and execute no instructions in the cached eight-core instruction model, within the design's performance budgets.
prediction: Budgets (baseline -> budget): SGIs to idle secondaries per tick with no ready task 7 (counted) -> 0, measured by the sgis counters in checks/a733-smp-cached.py and the QEMU eight-core model over 64 ticks; instructions per idle secondary between wake-ups: its full emulation quantum (counted: spin) -> 0 in WFI, with the idle loop growing by at most 6 instructions; core 0 idle wake-ups per second 1,000 -> 1,000; added work per tick in xTaskIncrementTick 0 -> one list-length compare (disassembly). Reasoning: before the change both FreeRTOS idle hooks were disabled so idle tasks spun, and core 0's time-slice check in xTaskIncrementTick yielded every core running an idle task because the idle-priority ready list always holds all eight idle tasks: 7 SGI0 interrupts and 7 context switches per tick with no work (counted).

conditions.base: commit 14c3cd8, the merge base of the package with the integration branch
conditions.package: commit 8072abf: adds the idle function in include/a733_cpu_power.h, its check and its documentation. No image included the header at that commit, so the model measurement applied the image change as a patch to the staged tree
conditions.builds: both trees configured with the project clang 21 toolchain and the pinned FreeRTOS kernel; integrated OS image built with SUNSTONE_A733_OS=ON and SUNSTONE_A733_OS_RESIDENT=ON
conditions.workload: checks/cpu-power-states-idle.c replaces the cached image's diagnostic: one task per secondary core blocks on a notification while the core 0 task sleeps for 64 ticks; the check counts SGIs, timer wake-ups and executed instructions per core over that window, then requires every secondary task to wake for a notification and for a two-tick delay
conditions.model: instruction model of checks/a733-smp-cached.py; no board executed either image

conclusion: All budgets pass except the static instruction count in xTaskIncrementTick, which grows by 24 instructions (96 bytes) instead of one list-length compare: the compiler unrolls the time-slice loop over the eight cores and each core's iteration adds CMP, MOV and CSINC to select the idle-priority threshold beside the existing list-length compare, with no memory access added. docs/cpu-power.md records this excess; in an idle system the 24 register instructions per tick replace seven SGIs and seven context switches per tick. The model has no A733 power, cache or interconnect timing, so the figures show interrupts sent and instructions executed, not energy or wake-up latency.
narrative: Results table (budget / base / package with image change / within budget): SGIs to idle secondaries per tick, no ready task: 0 / 4.47 (295 in 66 ticks) / 0 (0 in 64 ticks) / yes. Instructions per idle secondary in the window: 0 / 328,857 to 597,773 / 0 / yes. Instructions on core 0 in the window: not budgeted / 463,508 / 70,551. Core 0 timer wake-ups per second: 1,000 / 1,000 / 1,000.7 / yes. Instructions per idle-loop iteration, passive and active: at most 6 more / 3 and 4 / 5 and 6 / yes. Static instructions in xTaskIncrementTick: one list-length compare / 241 / 265 / no. Integrated OS image allocated bytes: no growth / 10,850,228 / 10,850,228 / yes. The base window spans 66 ticks because the core 0 task wrote its end marker two ticks late. The 1,000.7 per second comes from 64 timer interrupts over the model's clock count for the window; the model advances its clock in fixed steps, so the rate is 1,000 within one step. Idle loops: prvPassiveIdleTask is 7 instructions in the base (loop LDR, CMP, B.LO) and 10 with the image change (loop adds DSB SY, WFI); prvIdleTask is 11 instructions (loop BL, LDR, CMP, B.LO) and 14 (loop adds DSB SY, WFI). The added DSB SY is one barrier per idle wake-up, permitted before WFI by section 1.2 of docs/performance-architecture.md; the base loop spins without a barrier and never stops. Image size: at the package commit no image includes the new header, so the integrated OS image is unchanged; its .text, .data, .bss and .rodata sizes match the base, .text and .data are byte-identical, and the only differing allocated bytes are the 32-byte build identity in .rodata, which hashes the source tree. With the image change applied, the cached diagnostic image keeps its .text and .bss sizes; its function bytes grow by 140, which section alignment absorbs, and its .rodata grows by 24 bytes because assertion messages name the patched tasks.c by a longer build path. Reproduce: run checks/cpu-power-states.py with --evidence DIR --freertos PINNED_FREERTOS --source BASE_TREE --record-only to record the base metrics without applying the budgets, then with --patch IMAGE_CHANGE to apply the budgets; it passes when idle secondaries receive no SGI and execute no instruction over the window and still wake for work (PATH=$HOME/.cache/sunstoneos/host/usr/lib/llvm-21/bin:$PATH, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, ~/.cache/sunstoneos/venv/bin/python).

hypothesis: a733_cpu_idle (DSB SY, WFI) on core 0 of the single-core platform wakes on every 1 ms scheduler tick and the PMU cycle counter stops while the core waits.

conditions.task: one task at EL1 called a733_cpu_idle with IRQs unmasked

conclusion: 1,000 wakes over 1,000 ticks in 1.0 s of the 24 MHz counter; the longest gap between wakes was 24,001 counter ticks (1.0 ms), so no tick was missed. PMCCNTR_EL0 advanced 841,417 cycles over that second, 0.17% of 494 million: the A55 cycle counter stops while the core waits in WFI, so it measures only the active time of a core that idles in WFI, and idle time is the elapsed counter time less the active cycles. Each wake costs about 841 cycles and 316 instructions for the tick handler and the task's loop. The run does not cover EL0 WFI with nTWI, SGI0 wakes or the eight-core scheduler.
narrative: Run on port 3-3, core 0, on 2026-10-24, in bundle 4 of docs/designs/board-bundles-next.md; raw log ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/board-session-20261023/port-3-3/bb4-run/kernel.log.

hypothesis: Hardware record of the secondary core power-off and power-on sequence through EL3.
narrative: Per-step board status of the sequences that the deferred core power-off design would use. CPU_ON: require PPU status OFF (0x07052008 + n*0x1000, bits 3:0 = 0); write and verify entry words (0x08001004, 0x08001008 + n*0x1000) and AArch64 bit 0 of 0x08001000 + n*0x1000; set mode bit 0 (0x07050220 + n*4), then control bit 0 (0x07050200 + n*4); wait for status 8 (ON); restore control and mode. Sources: published board monitor helpers at file offsets 0xc4a0, 0xc298, 0xc314; TF-A A733 sunxi_pwr_domain_on (InfernoEmbedded/arm-trusted-firmware@5bc9605, plat/allwinner/common/sunxi_native_pm_ncat2.c); implemented as platform/a733/cpu_start.c. Board: first power-on passes on every secondary; a second power-on in one boot is unproven. CPU_OFF GIC part: disable CPU-interface groups; set GICR_WAKER.ProcessorSleep; wait for ChildrenAsleep (Arm IHI 0069G GICR_WAKER; TF-A gicv3_rdistif_mark_core_asleep); passes with delivery disabled (native-wake-sleep-20261018). CPU_OFF core part: set CPUPWRCTLR_EL1.CORE_PWRDN_EN, DSB, ISB (Cortex-A76 erratum 2743102); clear mode bit 0; set control bit 1 (GIC wake-up disable); DSB SY; WFI (TF-A cortex_a55_core_pwr_dwn, cortex_a76_core_pwr_dwn at ARM-software/arm-trusted-firmware@0892ad4; TF-A A733 sunxi_cpu_off; monitor helper at 0xc2f0); passes in startup diagnostics on every secondary (secondary-local-probe-20261018/physical-110). Warm entry GIC: clear control bit 1; wake the redistributor; configure SGI0 (platform/a733/cpu_continue.c; TF-A sunxi_pwr_domain_on_finish; monitor helper at 0xc224); passes for cold entry only. Both TF-A power-down functions issue no cache maintenance before WFI, so they rely on hardware cleaning of the private caches; the Cortex-A55 r2p0 and Cortex-A76 r4p1 manuals must confirm this before any code. The published monitor also clears the low four bits of nine undocumented registers at 0x07051000-0x07059000 (file offset 0x4e88). Cluster facts: the A733 has one DynamIQ cluster holding all eight cores (user manual section 5.1.5.4, printed page 250: C0_CPU0 to C0_CPU7 under one C0_RST_CTRL; figure 5-1 shows one L3 and snoop filter).
